text:
alex: heads-up — canary rollout for v2.9.1 is showing a p95 jump on small/medium seqs after the kernel-selector change. metrics in perfgate flagged it at 06:12 UTC :eyes:
perf-bot: ALERT perfgate/kv-midseq-tail failed (p95 78ms > threshold 50ms) — run: ci-1879
alex: repro locally with the short KV suite. saw similar p95 increases. suspect the new kernel heuristic prefers the aten_opt path which regresses for midseqs under our batching patterns.
priya: can you paste the bench output?
alex: sure — snippet:
```
p95_latency_ms baseline: 42.1 -> canary: 78.3 (+86%)
median_latency_ms baseline: 18.4 -> canary: 20.1 (+9%)
cpu% baseline: 60 -> canary: 72
kernel_path: chosen=aten_opt (heuristic v3) fallback=aten_scalar
batch_size_distribution: {1:40%, 2:35%, 3+:25%}
```
jun: interesting that median is mostly stable but tail blows up. suggests contention or a non-linear cost in aten_opt for certain sequence lengths. could be KV cache interaction.
matt: i captured a profile flamegraph for a slow sample — attaching inline summary: high time in `gemm_sparse_fallback` called from `aten_opt_transform`.
sara: did we change the kernel scoring formula in the selector PR? iirc it added a tiny weight for memory locality.
alex: yes — commit 0f3a9b2 added `locality_bonus` and raised aten_opt score for gpu-shared-local cases.
priya: that PR also changed continuous batching heuristics?
alex: the batcher tweak was independent, but timing overlap means more multi-request batches hit aten_opt with mixed seq lengths.
jun: can we bisect quickly? if the change is 0f3a9b2 then we can test with selector reverted locally to confirm.
priya: running quick bisect: `git checkout HEAD~3 && ./scripts/bench/kv_suite.sh --tag=ci-bisect`
perf-bot: queued job ci-bisect-42 on runner-8 (ETA ~7m)
deploy-bot: canary paused for safety — manual hold by deploy-bot at 06:25 UTC (reason: perfgate failure) :no_entry_sign:
alex: results from local revert: p95 back to 44ms. confirms selector change is main cause.
matt: ok that narrows it. next steps: either tune selector scoring or add a defensive check in runtime to avoid aten_opt for certain midseq+mixed-batch shapes.
sara: also we should improve CI coverage — current kv-midseq-tail test only runs on PRs sporadically and is flaky. let's add a deterministic micro-benchmark that simulates mixed batching patterns and captures tail percentiles.
priya: propose new test: `perfgate/kv-mixed-batching-tail` with 30 iters, seeded RNG, run on every PR and canary. thresholds: p95 < 55ms, p99 < 120ms.
jun: note: thresholds tuned for current infra (A100-40GB). add a gating tolerance flag to perfgate so infra jitter doesn't block unrelated changes.
alex: also discovered one KV-cache eviction pattern that amplifies the cost: when a batch contains a long and several short seqs, aten_opt's kernel creates temporary tensors that trigger cuda-memcpys. profiling: `cudaMemcpy 12.3ms` spikes correlating with p95 samples.
matt: fix options: 1) revert selector weight (short-term), 2) restrict aten_opt to single-seq batches, 3) improve kernel to avoid memcopy hotspot (longer-term).
sara: given rollout hold, we should revert the selector change to unblock customers and open a follow-up to implement a robust selector test + kernel fix.
priya: +1. i'll open a revert PR with a clear changelog and link to this thread.
priya: PR draft: `revert: selector locality bonus (0f3a9b2)` — will request quick review from @matt and @alex.
perf-bot: perfgate run scheduled: perfgate/kv-mixed-batching-tail (ci-1880) — threshold p95 55ms p99 120ms
jun: parallel action: i'll start a perf branch to instrument kernel scoring telemetry (emit chosen path, computed scores, batch stats) so we can run large-sample validation in staging.
alex: also adding a CI harness change: run the new test 3x in job with median-of-3 to reduce flakes and surface true regressions.
matt: can we tweak alerting to only fire after 2 consecutive failures in perfgate to reduce noisy pauses?
sara: agreed. add that to perfgate config and note in the retro.
priya: revert PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/revert-selector-0f3a9b2 — tagging @eng-runtime for urgent review :shipit: 
alex: thanks. after revert lands we'll re-run the canary and if stable, resume rollout. then follow-up work: kernel patch + new perf test + telem. assign owners: kernel fix @matt, telemetry @jun, perfgate test + thresholds @priya, revert review @sara.
perf-bot: ACTION logged: PERF-3892 "selector change rollback + new kv-mixed-batching-tail test" assigned to priya,matt,jun (priority P0)
sara: adding retro note: tighten perfgate thresholds, add median-of-3 reruns, and document batching-shape unit test patterns.
alex: cool. thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the runbook for followups. i'll post updates as PRs merge. :thumbsup:
